Journey Girls 18" Doll, Meredith The Journey Girls dolls are 18" dolls. Clothing-wise, they appear to be compatible with other 18" dolls such as American Girl, Playtime by Eimmie, the Our Generation dolls, or even the 18" Adora dolls. At this price point, they are definitely an affordable play option for younger girls. Like the Adora dolls, they have plastic shoulder and upper torso area and the lower torso is cloth. (The AG, Playtime by Eimmie, and Our Generation dolls all have completely cloth torsos). The Journey Girls dolls do not turn their head well, but their face sculpts are all unique to each doll (again, similar to the Adora dolls, as the Playtime by Eimmie seem to all have the same face sculpt with different skin shades and paint jobs). I personally find the Adora dolls to be my favorite 18" alternative to the American Girl dolls, but they are still at a high enough price point that I would not want to hand one over to my 5 year old for unsupervised play. The Playtime by Eimmie dolls have a full cloth body, making them softer and more huggable than the Journey Girls dolls (and probably more appealing for younger girls), and they are about the same price point. The style of clothing the Journey Girls have, as well as their sculpted plastic upper torsos, they give the impression of teenagers rather than younger girls, which makes them very appealing to the 8-10 year old set.

Meredith is absolutely beautiful and my daughters love her glamorous clothing and hairstyle. An affordable 18" doll option that doesn't make me cringe to give to impulsive young girls for play.
text_fidelity_b: Journey Girls 18" Doll, Meredith

Mattel Games Pictionary: Frame Game I was really excited about this product, as Pictionary is one of my all-time favorite party games. This was a disappointment on so many levels.

First, there is no storage box. It comes with a frame, a frame stand, a timer, and a marker. And a dice, which got lost in no time. The "frame" itself is about the size of a sheet of paper (8" by 10"), and it is clear, so you can see through it. The small size makes it ideal for travel or a backpack, but the fact that it is clear makes it difficult to see when holding it on your lap. And forget about using it on the black coffee table. It works much better when used flat, on a light background surface. I like that you can use the frame as a window, so the see-through feature may be useful one at a time. It's pretty much impossible for two people to write on opposite sides of the board at the same time. Honestly it is pretty much for anyone to write on the board when it is in the stand, which keeps the board vertical.

We like to use large dry-erase boards when we pay Pictionary. I would recommend that rather than this game. The frame might be fun to draw on once in a while -- but shy not get a small whiteboard, which is much better suited for the purpose?
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games Pictionary: Frame Game

text_fidelity_a:
eeBoo French Flash Cards I had the great fortune of parents who made sure I learned three other languages as a kid. They started very early with me and I distinctly remember them making their own flashcards. It's too bad that they didn't have access to these beautiful, affordable, and very easy to use flashcards to aid them! Now, as a parent, teacher, and a nanny, I work hard to teach my kids the basics of French and Spanish, and I stumbled across these. They have been well worth the price and they were highly affordable. Best of all, my kids that I teach love the cards and enjoy using them too. I would recommend them to both the beginner and the advanced speaker as they embark on teaching others.

There are a few times that the cards use outdated pronunciations or word choices, but it's actually a plus in my book because it aids further in teaching. When I see a card with a different context of pronunciation or word choice than what is currently popular or commonly used, then I can supplement by saying "Or you could say it like this ..." text_fidelity_a:
NERF Thunderhawk Nerf AccuStrike Mega Toy Blaster - Longest Nerf Blaster - 10 Official AccuStrike Nerf Mega Darts, 10-Dart Clip, Bipod My boys(5, 7, and 10) love Nerf guns. It's been a main request for birthdays and Christmas over the past year. For my 10 year old's last birthday, he requested a Nerf war. It was beyond fun to see the adults(of all ages) getting in on the fun right alongside the children. This one has a cool factor, since it's the longest Nerf gun at the moment and it truly is Mega. You can slide the barrel out to make it longer and slide it back in to make it shorter. It also has a bipod.

On the negative side, it takes up a great deal of room. It's a bit of a pain with its size. It's also so big that it's hard for my boys to use. I tried to use it and it's even awkward for me. I'd recommend this gun more for teens and adults. The only way my boys are really able to use it is with the bipod. It is a bit easier in the shorter length, but it's still heavy and awkward.

It also takes larger bullets than the average Nerf gun. It's a pain to have to worry about buying 2 separate kinds of bullets. All the rest of what we have take the same ones, and it makes things simpler. This gun comes with 10, but my boys lose darts constantly. Many times we discover where they were after the lawnmower turns them to confetti. Prepare for an extra investment if you don't already have other Mega guns.

Overall, if you don't mind buying the bigger bullets that go with this one and you or your child can handle the size, it's a pretty cool gun. My boys have had a hard time overly enjoying it, though, even if they do find it cool.

HobbyZone Champ RTF, HBZ4900 This is a great little plane, no question. But I ignored Hobbyzone's recommendation for 14 years old and up. I bought two: one for each of my 9-year-old twin sons, who were hot to fly RC model airplanes. One learned to fly quickly, but the other has been seriously disappointed. And I had to learn quickly how to use styrofoam glue to reattach broken wings, tail parts, motor mounts, etc.

It took me a while to understand how critical the trim really is: a beginner really can't fly a plane that isn't trimmed properly. You can get the trim in the ballpark with visual inspection of the control surfaces, but to get it right you have to fly the plane yourself. When I did that, and touched up the trim, flying became a lot of fun - for one boy. The other boy still can't fly more than a few seconds before landing his plane on its nose. He has just about given up in disgust.

I suspect that in a year or two both boys will have good flying skills. But in the meantime one boy is ready to move up while the other is ready to give up. Bummer!

text_fidelity_a:
Cosco Funsport Deluxe Play Yard, Monster Syd Comes packed in a nice sturdy box. Inside the play yard is in a nice nylon bag.
Just pull the 2 velcro straps open, take off the wrap around/bottom part of play yard, pop the play yard open, insert bottom pad.
It wasn't until I was packing this back up that I found the instructions. They are in a small pocket that's on the wrap around/bottom pad part of play pen. With that said, we had a little trouble getting this set up but, finally got it figured out without instructions.
When opening, before you push the middle part of the bottom down, straighten and lock the side rails up. If you open it up all the way, the two smaller sides won't lock into place. Pull the red strap back up a bit then click them and push the bottom back down.

The bottom pad is a bit thin and it's a little shorter than the play yard is. Nothing that I would take a star away for.
Once set up, it seems sturdy enough to keep a small child safe.
There is nice padding around the entire top. Even the release buttons are under the padded top rail so there's no chance of child pinching any fingers.
Has nice plastic wheels on one side so you can easily lift one side and roll it to another location.
The top arching top attachment is cute with 2 small monsters attached to it. It just snaps onto the side rails and is nice and flexible. Not sure how much abuse that can withstand. And not sure what a bigger child would do to it if they were jumping in it.
Packing it back up was just a little difficult. Have to make sure the side rails are completely released so it closes up nicely to be packed. Nothing to complain about. Do it a few times and it will be a breeze.
The bottom pad wraps around the play yard. Put velcro straps through opening, pull tight, and push the velcro into place.
Slips back easily into nylon packing bag.
Nylon bag also has a couple handles for easy carrying and I can slip it onto a bike hook and hang it in the garage so it doesn't take up floor space.
This is a great play pen/play yard for a young child. Can toss it into the car and bring it anywhere you might need it.
I think the price is a great price for what you're getting.
I really don't have any complaints with this.
text_fidelity_b: Cosco Funsport Deluxe Play Yard, Monster Syd

text_fidelity_a: Halloween Lights- 24 pcs Halloween LED Necklace Bracelets Pumpkin Ghost Pirate Spider Eyeball Necklace Halloween Party Favor Light up Flashing Decoration Trick Treats Gift Bag Fillers for Women Men Family Pack There are 24 different Halloween themed pieces in the box, ranging from pumpkins, to ghosts, to pirate ships, to spiders, to skulls.  The necklaces have a simple snap clasp at the end, and the bracelets have two different size settings.  The lights have three different colors including red, green, and blue.  There are three different setting to the lights with how they flash.  When first turned on, all three of the colors work great.  All the red, green and blue lights work at first.  But after about 10 minutes, the blue light starts to fade, then the green light starts to fade, until only the red light is working.  If turned off and left to sit and rest for a while, then all three light begin to light up and work again, but eventually again only the red light will remain lit.  This happened with all of the necklaces and bracelets in the box.  So as long as the lights are not needed to stay on for long periods of time, they are nice.  If needed for longer periods, two bracelets or necklaces or one of each could be used to alternate between them to give each one a rest by turning it off to refresh the colors.  So if handing these out for Halloween treats, I would recommend giving kids two in order to compensate for the lights not working all the time.
text_fidelity_b: Halloween Lights- 24 pcs Halloween LED Necklace Bracelets Pumpkin Ghost Pirate Spider Eyeball Necklace Halloween Party Favor Light up Flashing Decoration Trick Treats Gift Bag Fillers for Women Men Family Pack

Pass the Stache Board Game The purpose of this game is pretty much to match "moustaches" with cards. Each player picks a "moustache" and holds it under their nose during the game. When a card is turned over that matches their chosen "moustache", they slam it down on the card, causing the attached suction cup to attach to that card.

It's a great memory game! If the player smashes the wrong card, they lose 2 of their winning cards. Each player has to remember which one(style and color) they have under their nose. It's also great for motor skills, since they have to aim for the card, possibly in a race against another person.

I was pleasantly surprised at how sturdy the "moustaches" actually are. (The handles remind me of a kitchen spoon/spatula handle.) The "moustaches" are larger than I expected and they're a sturdy rubber material. There are 6 different shapes/styles in 3 different colors(black, yellow, and brown).

I've had lots of fun playing this game with my newly 6 year old(delayed) and my 3 year old. My 19 month old has had fun, too, but he doesn't play by the rules. ;) This is a great game for some family fun. Laughs are pretty much guaranteed!

text_fidelity_a:
Tokaido Board Game (Base Game) | Strategy Game | Travel Adventure Game | Exploration Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 8+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Funforge Simple, serene and elegant, this is a game like few others in your collection. This one is about a trip through Japan, and has very nice Japanese style artwork that really pops. One look at the box cover will tell you how elegant and evocative this game is, and that really is one of it's finest features.

Gameplay is rather simple. Those who rush ahead to see the sights first certainly get some kind of advantage - they often get first choice of where to go - while those who take their time will have plenty of opportunity to catch up, as the last player is always the next to move, meaning that travellers who venture too far out will allow others to make every stop along the way. There are "safe" and predictable options where you always get two or three points, and there are gambling options where you might be able to buy cards that give you far more.

It's a good, simple game that works well as a gateway game, but like many games, it says it's a decent two-player game, and I don't think that it is. It shines with three to four players. The decisions are not particularly deep or exciting, and much of the time, there really are only two choices that you can choose from - move really slow, or move really fast - and those choices are often easy to make.

If you're a gamer, I don't think you'll like this game. You can find better gateway games for sure, and there are thousands of games where you'll make more interesting choices. If you're just getting into games, or if you need something new to play with grandma, then this might be the best choice you can make.
text_fidelity_b: Tokaido Board Game (Base Game) | Strategy Game | Travel Adventure Game | Exploration Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 8+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Funforge

Great Gift for Mom, Dad, Teens, Men and Women I could not tell exactly how these “puzzles” work, even after looking at the video. You have to do two different things. First you have to “flip” each of the circles back-and-forth until you get all of them flipped to the correct side. Then you have to “spin” each of the circles to align them correctly. I find that it’s best to start from the outside circle and work your way in. The “puzzles” with most similar colors / designs on each side are the most challenging to work to get the circles on the correct side.

FYI. . . Once you have completed one side, the opposite side will not be complete. So though you will not have to flip the circles. . You’ll have to rotate the circles to complete the puzzle. So you’ll always have one side complete, and one size incomplete.

It should be noted that this “puzzle” is sturdy enough for a puzzle such as this, but it can certainly be pulled apart and broken without too much effort.

I think this “puzzle” to be best for ages tweens and up. It’s not super challenging, but again the ones with the common colors on both sides are the most challenging.

This puzzle is Made in China and being sold by a Canadian company on Amazon.

text_fidelity_a:
Cephalofair Games: Gloomhaven, Award-Winning Strategy Board Game, For 1 to 4 Players, 60 to 120 Minute Play Time, For Ages 14 and up I purchased this game while it was on sale, and after playing it for ~20 hours, I would gladly have paid double for the experience. While it is true that it can be a bit intimidating at first for most people, after the initial steep learning curve is over this game really begins to shine. Unlike other legacy games, Gloomhaven is more forgiving in the sense that you don't actually lose anything, but rather you learn from your mistakes and get to try again without penalty.

Even if you don't have other friends who would be willing to play with you, playing by yourself (controlling two characters at once) is incredibly fun and engaging. I would recommend playing with 2 to 3 people though.

My only gripe with the game is that it doesn't include any real solution for organizing the game once you start playing. I would highly recommend Broken Token's Gloomhaven organizer as well as the removable sticker sheet. The BT organizer may be expensive as well, but it's worth every penny.
text_fidelity_b: Cephalofair Games: Gloomhaven, Award-Winning Strategy Board Game, For 1 to 4 Players, 60 to 120 Minute Play Time, For Ages 14 and up

TEAM MAGNUS 18ft XL Slip and Slide - Heavy Duty Inflatable Slide with Central Sprinkler and XL Crash Pad I’ve used the slide on a slight slope and almost a flat surface. PRO’s: width and length of slide (twice as long as other slides in target audience), easy setup/operate/put away, splash zone (pool at end) works to stop toddlers. CON’s: the streaming water that “wets” the slide is too wide near the end of the slide and hardly existing at the start of the slide. The splash zone edges (inflated) nearest to the slide don’t ensure participant won’t slide over and miss splash zone.
A simple design improvement would be to have far less watering holes for the slip and slide near the splash zone and progressively more as you near the starting point. This to be is the largest flaw in the slide.
There are ways to “work around” the lack of water on the slide (the lack of slipperiness) but the product should fix this vs the customer having workarounds.

text_fidelity_a:
My Arcade GameStation Wireless - Plug and Play Game Console - 2 Wireless Controllers - 300 Retro Style Games - Battery or USB Powered - Plugs Into TV I like this game console, but really just think it's something that a few people will enjoy more than most. The design of the console is really good, the look of the main unit is very well done. The wireless controllers are decent enough and feel well made. It's the games though that count. The games are a bit underwhelming. There is a good variety of games, from card games (solitaire, go fish, and a few others of that kind) to puzzle games (sudoku, sliding block puzzle, a pattern block puzzle). There are also many arcade style games. This model of the console does not have any of the old Data East arcade games on it. There is another version that does. The front of the box for that one will have graphics showing the Data East games.

I was sort of expecting the games on this to be the same as what is on most of these sort of consoles (famiclone games), but instead these are a bit more generic than even those. Some of the games are difficult to figure out, it took me about 10-15 minutes or experimenting to figure out how the controllers worked with the sudoku game, and even after I did - the controls were so awkward it made playing the game nearly impossible (and given that this game is timed, I never could achieve a decent time in solving the puzzle). Still, there are many that are worth playing. I think one of the reasons I like game systems like this is the challenge of figuring out what makes the game work.

The main game unit take four double A batteries and the wireless units take triple-A batteries (three each). The console hooks to the TV via a composite video cable (yellow RCA plug) and has one audio input (another RCA plug). I'm using the front inputs on my old VCR which is still connected to my television. I like that the controllers are wireless. You don't really need both, many of the games are for single player. The controllers are marked (P1 & P2), as the P1 controller is the main one and it is used to select the games from the menu.

All-in-all, I am enjoying most of these games, and appreciate the game system for what it is - but I would imagine that many people might not.

This system is made by My Arcade Gaming, and I have one of their handheld Go Gamer Portable games which I purchased last year around Christmas time. I was sort of hoping that this new game console would have the same set of games on it that their handheld model has (which are really good by the way), but that wasn't the case.
text_fidelity_b: My Arcade GameStation Wireless - Plug and Play Game Console - 2 Wireless Controllers - 300 Retro Style Games - Battery or USB Powered - Plugs Into TV

text_fidelity_a:
Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig [[VIDEOID:f267642283bcf2ef6b127013dc46be9b]] On the advertising, this says that it shoots 20 feet. I was really skeptical, and I was expecting it to only shoot 20 feet in the air. Now, I don't have a 20 foot ladder, so I can't tell for sure, but I'm pretty sure that this will shoot vertically 20 feet, and horizontally maybe even a little more.

The truck is big and bulky, which I really liked. And there are no small, removable parts, so it's probably good for kids of any age. It does shoot a pretty powerful stream of water, so the only danger is squirting friends, family, and pets in the eye.

Now, about the water, the truck doesn't hold very much water. It says that it will shoot 50 shots of water, and it does do that. This is a lot like one of those water conserving showers. It really doesn't use very much water, but you can't really tell that until you fill it up. So, it's not the best thing for a water fight. But it is a great gift for youngsters so they don't get their siblings too wet. And I did really like the bright, vivid colors.

The wheels rotate, but they can't turn. If you need to turn this, you'll need to pick it up and move it around. Really, the only movable part on this is the fire hose.

Pros:
+Big and bulky
+Fun for all ages
+Shoots water a long way
+You can position the fire hose a little

Cons:
-A little hard to aim
-Wheels can't turn right or left, only rotate straight ahead
-Doesn't hold a ton of water
-You can't build up pressure to do a power squirt
text_fidelity_b: Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig

text_fidelity_a:
The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe) The resistance is a fantastic game with a great price and superb components. The rules are very simple also so the game can be picked up by nearly anyone in a matter of minutes. A sample round will remove any doubt about the rules and is often the best way I have found to teach the game.

So what is this about? The Resistance is a game of guessing and deduction that is rules light and fun heavy. In the basic game 5 to 10 players take on the role of either good guys or bad guys by being dealt cards that depict their character. Good guys or the resistance are blue and spies are red. The ratio of spies to resistance is driven by the number of players in a game. The spies always have fewer allies in the game than do the resistance players.

Once the players have secretly looked at their role card, everyone closes their eyes. The first player commands everyone to close their eyes, he then commands the spies and only the spies to open their eyes and look around to identify each other, he then commands them to close their eyes and lastly commands everyone to open their eyes.

So now the spies know who each other are but the allies have no idea.

The game is then played as 5 simple 'missions'. A mission consists of the first player choosing a number
of players to 'go on the mission'. The number is dependent on how many total players are playing. The more players, the more involved in each mission. Each mission from 1 to 5 will have gradually more players involved.

Everyone votes to allow or disallow the chosen players to go on the mission. Each player will have two cards to vote
with each round. These cards are marked clearly with symbols to indicate if you do or do not agree to allow the chosen players to play.

Here is where the game gets going. If the vote fails to allow the chosen players to go on the mission twice in a row, the spies win automatically.

If the players allow the mission to go forward, those players involved get to either make the mission successful or to sabotage the mission. This is done my dealing each player involved in the mission two cards. One of each success and sabotage. They secretly place their cards into two piles. The mission result and the dead pile.

Spies can sabotage or succeed a mission and the resistance players MUST succeed the mission.

The majority of succeed of sabotage rules the mission.

Rounds continue like this until the spies or the resistance have a best 3 out of 5 missions won by their side.

Up until this point your first game might seem kinda boring. But just wait, almost immediately you will figure
out who your junior sleuths are! Finger pointing and accusations will begin to fly out of the most timid players
mouths!

You will find players who are just 100% certain they know who is who and are almost always wrong! You will find out that some of your friends are REALLY GREAT LIARS and some are REALLY POOR LIARS!

The compound the fun there is also a plot deck. The plot deck is simply a deck of cards that each round, one is dealt by the first player and he can give it to someone else or keep it.
These cards are things like 'look at someone else role card' or 'veto a vote'.

I initially thought the plot deck would be horrible but I was very wrong. The first time we pulled a card that let one player look at another players role card the player looked and claimed the other player was a spy. The player accused immediately did a double take and denied the allegation fervently!

We were back at square one but now had two more people we couldn't trust! FUN! FUN! FUN!

You cannot go wrong with this game unless you live in a convent full of people with ZERO personality who have had all their fun genes removed.

So if you are looking for an excellent game, with super components, short playing time, and an immeasurable amount of fun, look no further than this gem!
text_fidelity_b: The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe)

Overall, it's fun to play with. I think younger girls would have a blast with it, and I do think they are its target age group. I feel like the price is a bit much for what it does, though.

Prextex Pack of 2 Wind up Bubble Machine Toy Gun Shooter LED Light up Bubbles Blower Indoor and Outdoor Toys for Kids and Toddler - no Batteries Needed | Great Gift Set for Birthdays I bought two packs of these bubble guns for a birthday party. You receive 2 pink guns and 3 blue guns in each pack. They are clear and have noise and lights.

Of the 10 bubble guns I received, 2 were defective. There is a lever that moves up and down to produce the bubbles. The lever is supposed to move when the trigger is pressed. For one of the defective bubble guns the lever was so tight that it rarely moved hence no bubbles. For the second defective bubble gun the rubber tubing was run the wrong way down the front of the gun so the rubber tube is very short. It produces bubbles but only when immersed in liquid in the bottle. It also spills a large amount of bubble liquid because of the defective tubing. After a short while it stops working because the bubble solution is too low in the bottle. My hand was also covered in solution at this point.

For the remainder of the bubble guns the rubber tubing is too long and they will not produce bubbles. The tubing is pressed against the side of the bubble container and is unable to siphon up the bubble liquid. The solution is to either push the tubing back up into the gun to make it about 1/4 inch shorter or to snip the end of the tubing by about 1/8 inch. The remaining 8 guns worked after I pushed the tubing higher.

I recommend you test the guns before handing them to children. I bought them for a birthday party so I tested them ahead of time to prevent disappointment.

These are different than battery operated bubble guns. For one thing, the lever has to be pressed about three times each time to produce bubbles in most of the bubble guns. For a few of the bubble guns a slow steady press produced a steady stream of bubbles but most of the triggers are too loose to allow a slow press. So the quality is inconsistent.

I paid $15.99 per box so from a value perspective I wasted about $6.36 because of the defective guns. I'll probably return one box.

UPDATE: Amazon shipped two replacement boxes but 5 of the 10 replacement guns were defective. I could not get them to work no matter how hard or long I tried. I shipped the defective bubble guns back. I will repeat my advice. Test each gun if you are using them for a party or event. Buy early enough so you have time to have replacements shipped to you. The ones that did work, worked beautifully. The kids enjoyed them.
text_fidelity_b: Prextex Pack of 2 Wind up Bubble Machine Toy Gun Shooter LED Light up Bubbles Blower Indoor and Outdoor Toys for Kids and Toddler - no Batteries Needed | Great Gift Set for Birthdays

I like the way it moves its entire axels to do its stunts. You can get a pretty good idea of hwo this moves if you look at the pictures. Simple, but effective. Seems like kids younger than 8 would like this; odd because they show small kids crawling on the floor using this, but say it is for ages 8 and up. Just watch they don't try to eat the batteries, I guess. It's not super fast, either, so older kids might get bored.

Anyway, they totally cheaped out on the battery setup. 400mAh?!?! Are you kidding me? Even the cheap, "included" versions of decent brands are 1100mAh, with good ones getting 2500mAh or more. And why the goofy charging setup? You have to take it out and then hook it to an oddball USB cable (so now you can't just use any USB cable you have laying around, you have to have this one on hand). They should just wire a higher capacity battery inside and add a micro-USB port like everybody else.
